method: field observation of behaviour (3 min before capture, observer at least 2 m away) on flyover versus non-flyover days
conditions: Free-living all-female parthenogenetic lizards at Fort Carson U.S. Army Installation, El Paso County, Colorado. Non-flyover sampling days 14-20 June 2021, flyover days 23-25 June 2021. Ground noise read with a data-logging sound reader when each lizard was captured: 30.1 to 55.8 dB on non-flyover dates, 33.9 to 112.2 dB during flyovers. The stimulus is real aircraft passing (noise plus any visual or wind cues), not a sound-only playback, and the two periods are different dates. The Methods report no total number of flyovers or meter distance. Same paper: corticosterone and ketones rose with flyovers, plasma glucose did not change. The text says lizards spent significantly less time assessing surroundings, yet the reader returned Table 3c with a flyover p of 0.104, so the assessing result is not filed.
